title: Arizona Innovation Map
subtitle: Learning about Arizona’s semiconductor industry through a map.
html:
Open Arizona Innovation Map ↗

Project overview

After organizing the manufacturing stages in Arizona Chip Journey, I wondered what a fab needs beyond its own walls. I built Arizona Innovation Map from public sources to see where companies and institutions are located and what roles they play.

What I learned

I moved from knowing what a process needs to being able to describe what the surrounding businesses do. When I learned that wafer surface preparation uses chemicals and ultrapure water, for example, I began to distinguish material supply, equipment support, and facility services. I also learned to record what a company does, what its local site is used for, and what public sources can establish.

From a manufacturing step to a city

I grouped locations into semiconductor supply chain, business, and institutional categories. Filters for materials, equipment, facilities, and logistics help readers find sites and inspect their sources. Campuses, government offices, and selected businesses provide context for the communities around the fabs.

Local Phoenix 3D prototype

I brought company search, a list of sites, and a 3D map of Phoenix onto one page. Selecting a site shows its details alongside nearby cities, roads, and other locations. Approximate locations are labeled. Supplier, customer, or partnership relationships require separate evidence.
